implementation_notes: In the Akka ecosystem the pattern is delivered by Akka Management: a health check is a function returning Future[Boolean] (a class extending Function0[Future[Boolean]], optionally taking the ActorSystem), bound to readiness or liveness through akka.management.health-checks.readiness-checks / liveness-checks configuration, and HealthCheckRoutes serves /ready and /alive - returning 200 only when every configured check for that kind succeeds and 500 otherwise, with configurable paths. The registry therefore survives as configuration plus small classes, which is exactly where the pattern earns its keep: cluster membership, not just dependency reachability, can decide readiness (the cluster-membership check shipped with cluster-http management is the canonical example).
idiom_name: Akka Management HealthCheckRoutes (/ready and /alive) with configured Future[Boolean] checks
pitfalls: Checks are invoked on every probe: a check that blocks on I/O on the actor dispatcher starves the whole system, so run blocking work on a dedicated dispatcher and keep a timeout on the Future.
The endpoints only exist once Akka Management is started (AkkaManagement(system).start(), stopped in coordinated shutdown) - a service that forgets the lifecycle call has no probe at all.

A readiness check driven by cluster state flips the instance out of rotation while a rolling membership change is still in progress; thresholds and kind assignment (liveness vs readiness) decide whether that is protection or an outage.
